newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Selling depresses Nigerian share index.
newsitem.headline: Selling depresses Nigerian share index.

text.p: Heavy selling of shares in some of Nigeria's biggest companies depressed the stock market index on Tuesday.
The all-share index closed at 6,956.08 from 6,958.14 on Monday.
"The absence of any new information or corporate results further dampened enthusiasm in the market today," one trader said.
Dunlop fell 30 kobo to 9.00 naira, while Cadbury dropped the same amount to close at 22.20 naira.
Guaranty Trust Bank closed 20 kobo down at 11.70 naira. Traders said the shares were finding their level after an initial clamour after its September listing took it to 14.60 naira.
Traders priced Nigerian-German Chemicals Company 40 kobo lower at 8.30 naira because there were no buyers for the large volume on offer.
Positive movement was largely restricted to the oil marketing sector.
African Petroleum gained 30 kobo to 44.10 naira. Agip rose by the same margin to 22.50 naira. Unipetrol and National Oil climbed 20 kobo each to close at 56.70 naira and 45.70 naira respectively.
Nestle Foods remained in demand, closing 20 kobo higher at 48.00 naira.
Union Bank rose 25 kobo to 5.30 naira. Okomu Oil Palm finished 10 kobo up at 8.10 naira.
Conglomerate CFAO dropped 10 kobo to 2.53 naira. Ashaka Cement was down 10 kobo at 17.10 naira.
